items.followUp: Define a coordinate covalent bond and give an example involving the hydronium ion.

rubric.why: In a coordinate covalent bond, one atom supplies both electrons of the shared pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

rubric.why: Ammonium and hydronium ions are examples of coordinate covalent bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as NH4+ or H3O+.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.
Example: NH3 + H+ → NH4+; the nitrogen atom donates its lone pair.
